title: Armillary
concept: Three pierced discs stack on a plinth as a triple shutter over a ring of ten wells, and each well holds a face-down tile whose identity is carved on its underside — so what is hidden is not a passage you could squint down, it is a face lying on the floor of a well with its blank back turned up. A turn is: twist one disc up to three notches, see which wells now have all three windows lined up over them, then reach through and pull tiles one at a time — a star or a moon joins your catch, an eclipse ends your turn and dumps everything you took back onto the board face-up for the next player to help themselves to. The alignment you can see; what you are pulling out you cannot, and the disc you leave badly turned is the sky the next player has to work with.
novelty: The rework's core is that the hidden information is carried by one-sided relief lying face-down in a well — physically unpeekable rather than merely hard to see — while the open-information layer is a three-disc aperture whose alignment is the *skill*: rotating a disc sets both your own reach ceiling for a press-your-luck run and the next player's, so denying the table is an attack. Searches run: the mechanism verbatim ('three stacked rotating pierced discs act as a mask over a ring of face-down relief tiles, exposing only wells where all three windows align, and players press their luck revealing hidden tiles'), the incidental rule as its own pitch ('press your luck board game reveal hidden tiles until you draw a bust rotating aperture layers'), and the plain title query ('"Armillary" board game published'). Closest real prior art, and it is close on the object if not the game: Husker Du? (US, 1950s, BGG 14423) — a fixed pierced board over ONE dial of hidden pictures, all holes plugged by markers, lift two and match. It is a children's memory match-2 with a single dial the rules turn between rounds; here there are three independently player-rotated masks whose intersection is the whole tactical layer, no matching, a bust-and-forfeit push, and revealed eclipses that permanently clog wells and shrink the board. The press-your-luck query returned only the TV property and the generic BGG mechanic page, no aperture-gated variant. The title query returns 'Armillary Games', a Belgian publisher (its game is AstroNavigators, an unfunded 2025 campaign) and an unrelated Magic card 'Armillary Sphere' — a publisher name, not a shipped game title, so the name stays.

art_direction.form_language: Cast-bronze instrument, not machinery: a squat drum plinth with a heavy chamfered skirt, three flush-stacked pierced discs of the same diameter reading as one solid cylinder that has been drilled by a giant, and a tall square obelisk standing beside it. Everything is slab-thick — 6mm minimum on any disc, 9mm rims, no filigree, no thin spokes between windows.
art_direction.silhouette: A bronze astrolabe with an obelisk at its shoulder and four little racks of standing discs around it, like an observatory bench mid-session.
art_direction.part_vocabulary: plinth_ring is the only part with a skirt and a ring of sunken wells — unmistakable bulk; the three mask_discs share one outer silhouette on purpose but are told apart by grip-tab alone (broad rounded paddle / pointed triangular fin / notched double-prong), so a hand knows which layer it is turning without looking; the three tile families are deliberately IDENTICAL in outline, thickness, rim and back face — a 22mm round with a knurled pinch knob — and differ only in the relief carved on the face that lies downward, which is what makes them hideable at all; reserve_column is the only tall square part, an obelisk with a full-height read slot; score_rail is the only long low part, a stepped two-slot bar with a distinct polygonal finial per seat.
art_direction.surface_treatment: 1.2mm-deep constellation lines and dots engraved across the plinth's top face and each disc's upper face, continuing across window webs so the three layers read as one broken sky when aligned; 1.2mm raised sunburst collars ring the three zenith wells and repeat on the score_rail's raised slot; tile faces carry 1.2mm relief — a five-point star, a crescent, and an eclipse (a filled disc in a ring of radial notches); tile backs are dead flat with a knurled knob, and knurling is the only texture they carry.
art_direction.hero_shot: Overhead three-quarter, mid-run: a hand pinching a tile knob down through one aligned window, two star tiles already standing in the player's rail, an eclipse lying face-up in a sunburst-collared zenith well as a dead spot, and the obelisk's read slot showing the stack still half full.

components.name: plinth_ring
components.desc: 216mm-diameter, 30mm-tall drum with a chamfered skirt. Ten 24mm-diameter, 6mm-deep tile wells sunk on an 80mm-radius ring at 36-degree spacing, each with a thumb scallop; three of them (positions 0, 4 and 7) are ringed by a 1.2mm raised sunburst collar marking them as zenith wells. Central 24mm axle post rising 40mm. The well ring is recessed 6mm below the hub shoulder and the outer rim ledge that the disc stack rests on, so the stack floats clear of the tile knobs. Rim carries ten 1.2mm index grooves; top face carries 1.2mm constellation relief.

components.name: mask_disc_a
components.desc: Bottom mask: 216mm-diameter, 6mm-thick disc (9mm-thick outer rim band for stiffness), 25mm centre bore, free-turning on the axle post. Six 38mm-diameter windows on the same 80mm-radius ring at index positions 0,1,2,3,4,6. Broad rounded paddle grip-tab projecting 16mm past the rim, with a witness notch read against the plinth's index grooves.

components.name: mask_disc_b
components.desc: Middle mask: same 216mm/6mm profile, stacking directly on mask_disc_a. Six 38mm windows at index positions 0,1,2,3,6,7. Pointed triangular fin grip-tab, 16mm projection, own witness notch.

components.name: mask_disc_c
components.desc: Top mask: same 216mm/6mm profile, stacking on mask_disc_b. Six 38mm windows at index positions 0,1,3,5,6,8. Notched double-prong grip-tab, 16mm projection, own witness notch. The three patterns are chosen so that across all 100 relative rotations the number of fully aligned wells is never 0 and never more than 4 (typically 2, sometimes 3).

components.name: star_tile
components.desc: 22mm-diameter, 6mm-thick round with a 10mm-diameter, 9mm-tall knurled pinch knob on its back. Face carries a 1.2mm raised five-point star. Outline, thickness, rim and back are IDENTICAL to moon_tile and void_tile — the whole hidden-information layer depends on the three families being indistinguishable from every direction except the face, so no silhouette difference may be introduced.

components.name: moon_tile
components.desc: Same 22mm round, same knob, same back as star_tile; face carries a 1.2mm raised crescent.

components.name: void_tile
components.desc: Same 22mm round, same knob, same back as star_tile; face carries a 1.2mm eclipse — a filled disc inside a ring of radial notches. Revealing one busts a turn.

components.name: reserve_column
components.desc: Square obelisk, 46mm across a 70mm base and 150mm tall, with a 24mm round bore holding tiles stacked knob-up and a 9mm-wide full-height slot down one face so the remaining stack height is readable across the table as a game clock. Chamfered top mouth; tiles are drawn from the top.

components.name: score_rail
components.desc: 130mm x 30mm x 20mm bar with two parallel 6.6mm-wide, 11mm-deep slots that stand tiles on edge: a plain front slot and a raised rear slot on a stepped ledge marked with the sunburst collar motif, for zenith winnings. Each of the four rails carries a different end-finial cross-section — triangular, square, pentagonal, hexagonal prism — so a rail belongs to a seat by shape.

setup.text: Set the plinth_ring in the middle of the table and stack the masks on its axle post: mask_disc_a first, then mask_disc_b, then mask_disc_c. Turn all three so that every witness notch points at the plinth's index groove 0.
Turn all thirty tiles knob-up so no face is showing, then mix them by sliding them around the table without lifting or tilting any of them. Nobody may look at a face during this step.
Still without looking at faces, drop one tile knob-up into each of the ten wells of the plinth_ring, and stack the remaining twenty knob-up in the reserve_column.
Each player takes one score_rail and sets it in front of their seat. Youngest player goes first; play passes clockwise.

turn.text: TURN THE SKY. Rotate exactly one mask disc of your choice by one, two or three index grooves, in either direction. This is compulsory and public — everyone can see which layer moved and how far. It is also the only lever you have on what the next player will be able to reach.

READ THE SKY. A well is OPEN if all three masks show a window over it, so that you can see down to the tile in it. Wells covered by any one of the three masks are shut for this turn. There are always between one and four open wells.

REACH. You may now take tiles one at a time, and after each one you choose to push on or stop. To take a knob-up tile, pinch its knob through the open window, lift it out and turn it face-up in the middle of the table for everyone to see before adding it to your catch — the pile of tiles you have taken this turn, kept in front of you, not yet banked. You may also take an already face-up star_tile or moon_tile from an open well; that take is free and carries no risk. You may only ever take from open wells.

BUST. If a tile you turn up is a void_tile, your turn ends at once. Lay that void_tile back in its own well face-up, where it stays for the rest of the game and blocks that well permanently, and return every tile in your catch face-up to the well it came from — you have scouted the sky for everybody else. If the void came out of a zenith well (one with a sunburst collar), also take one tile of your choice off your score_rail and put it back in the box.

BANK. If you stop before busting, or run out of open wells holding a takeable tile, stand every tile in your catch in your score_rail: tiles taken from a zenith well go in the raised rear slot, everything else in the front slot. Banked tiles are safe for the rest of the game except to a zenith bust.

CLEAR (only if stuck). If, right after your rotation, no open well holds any takeable tile at all, you may instead lift one face-up void_tile out of any well, open or shut, and return it to the box. That well counts as empty.

REFILL. At the end of your turn, fill every empty well with the top tile of the reserve_column, placed knob-up without looking at its face. Wells holding a face-up tile are not refilled. Then play passes clockwise.

end.text: The game ends at the end of the turn on which the reserve_column is empty and no well holds a knob-up tile — there is nothing left to gamble on. It also ends immediately if every one of the ten wells holds a face-up tile, the sky fully eclipsed.

win.text: Score your score_rail: each star_tile is worth 2, each moon_tile 1, and every tile standing in the raised zenith slot is worth 1 more. Highest total wins. On a tie, the tied player with the most star_tiles wins; if that ties too, the win is shared.
